body:
PROBLEM. The CI rail-freeze gate has no notion of ticket COMPLETION. `scripts/rails-guard-ci.mjs` builds the frozen-rail set by UNIONing the `rails` arrays of EVERY ticket in the trusted base `.adlc/tickets.json` (see the loop "for (const t of baseTickets) for (const r of t.rails ?? []) rails.push(r)"). It never consults whether a ticket is done. So once a ticket ships, its build-time sibling-freeze rails stay frozen indefinitely, blocking unrelated future work that legitimately touches those paths — until a human performs an admin edit on main (`ADLC_RAILS_BYPASS=1`, byte-splicing the ticket's `rails` to `[]`).

EVIDENCE (this is not hypothetical). During the opencode T30–T35 continuation the gap forced THREE separate operator-authorized admin rail lifts on main:
- T20/T21 (pi Phase 1) rails lifted after #118 merged (they froze plugins/adlc-opencode/** etc.).
- T22–T25 (pi Phase 2–3) narrowed (dropped plugins/adlc-opencode/**) after #121/#122, then
- T22–T25 rails lifted entirely when a later ticket (T34) needed to edit docs/ci/adlc-maintenance.yml, which they still froze via docs/ci/**.
Each lift is a manual, audited, error-prone byte-splice of the shared trust-root file.

GOAL. A completed ticket's rails should stop contributing to the frozen set automatically, so rails-guard only enforces rails for work that is still IN FLIGHT — without weakening enforcement for active tickets or opening a bypass (a ticket must not be able to mark ITSELF done to unfreeze its own rails mid-build).

DESIGN DIRECTION (the executor picks the concrete mechanism; both are acceptable if they meet the ACs):
Option A — completion-aware union: rails-guard-ci.mjs skips a base ticket's rails when that ticket has trusted completion evidence. "Completed" must be derived from a TRUSTED, HARD-TO-FORGE signal, NOT a self-declared ticket field (a builder could set status:done to unfreeze). Candidates, in order of trust: (a) the ticket's scope files are all present AND the ticket has a manifest `type: p5-complete` / `p6-acceptance-packet` entry in the base `.adlc/manifest.jsonl` (append-only, already CI-protected); (b) the ticket id appears in a merged-work ledger. The union skips a ticket iff its completion evidence is present in the BASE ref (never HEAD — same trust-root discipline the gate already uses for rails).
Option B — lifecycle field on rails that clears at P6: rails move to P3 rail-write time and are cleared when the ticket reaches P6 integrate, recorded in the manifest chain; rails-guard reads only currently-frozen (P3-written, not-yet-P6-cleared) rails.

Whichever: the change is to the ENFORCEMENT gate + its trust model, so it is security-sensitive — it must FAIL CLOSED (a ticket whose completion evidence is absent/ambiguous/unverifiable stays FROZEN), and it must be adversarially reviewed at P1→P2 (can a builder forge completion to unfreeze rails mid-build?).

=== ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA (each with a concrete verification) ===
AC1: A base ticket with TRUSTED completion evidence no longer contributes its rails to the frozen set — a PR that edits a path only that ticket froze PASSES rails-guard. (verify: unit test in scripts/test/rails-guard-ci.test.mjs — a completed-ticket fixture + a diff touching its rail path → exit 0.)
AC2: An IN-FLIGHT ticket (no completion evidence) still freezes its rails — the same edit is DENIED. (verify: same test file, in-flight fixture → exit 2.)
AC3: FAIL CLOSED on forge/ambiguity — a ticket that self-declares done (e.g. a status field) WITHOUT the trusted evidence stays frozen; unverifiable/partial evidence stays frozen. (verify: test asserts a forged-completion fixture still denies.)
AC4: No self-unfreeze mid-build — completion evidence is read from the BASE ref only (never HEAD), mirroring how rails-guard already reads the rail set, so a builder cannot add completion evidence in their own PR to unfreeze their rails. (verify: test that HEAD-only completion evidence does NOT lift the freeze.)
AC5: The manual admin-lift path is documented as no-longer-routine (docs/ci/rails-guard.yml comment or docs/integrations/*.md), and the recurring-lift history is retired. (verify: read the doc.)
AC6: Full suite green incl. the existing rails-guard-ci tests (verify: npm test exit 0).

NON-GOALS: retroactively editing historical tickets' rails (this fixes the mechanism, not the data); changing the in-session PreToolUse rail hook (this is the CI gate).

CONTEXT FILES: scripts/rails-guard-ci.mjs (the union loop + base-ref reading), scripts/test/rails-guard-ci.test.mjs, packages/runner/lib/assertions.mjs (phase-completion evidence model: type ?? gate, p5-complete/p6-acceptance-packet), .adlc/manifest.jsonl (append-only, CI-protected). Memory: [[opencode-native-flush-build-state]] "OPEN SYSTEMIC GAP".
title: Rails completion lifecycle: a merged/completed ticket's rails must auto-expire, not freeze siblings forever
